subject: Edge storage + vector-sync partner pilot proposal
messages:
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
To: Emily Zhang <emily@pinecone.io>, Oscar Meier <oscar@weaviate.com>, Samir Gupta <samir@acme-storage.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 02 Aug 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Edge storage + vector-sync partner pilot proposal

Emily / Oscar / Samir —

Thanks again for taking time last week. Following our internal sync, I wanted to put a short, concrete pilot proposal on the table so we can all align on scope, success metrics, and timeline. High level: Redwood wants to validate a lightweight vector-sync pattern that keeps hot indexes on a managed vector DB (Pinecone / Weaviate) while allowing customers to spill and restore segments to S3-compatible object storage (Acme Storage) at the edge for cost and regional residency.

Attached is a one-page pilot-scope and a very rough SOW draft for legal/commercial intake. Key asks from each partner:
- Pinecone / Weaviate: a small dev cluster or sandbox project we can use for integration tests, and guidance on index migration semantics + TTL semantics.
- Acme (S3): access to a near-edge bucket and a short-term waiver on ingress egress costs for pilot traffic.
- Redwood: we will run the sync controller, provide observability hooks, and produce a short runbook + rollback plan.

Proposed success metrics (30-day pilot):
- End-to-end restore latency from S3 to vector index for a 1M-vector segment: < 6 minutes (90th pct)
- Token-per-second cost delta for retrieval flows compared to fully-provisioned index: <= 30% higher
- No data loss for staged spill/restore in two test failure scenarios (node loss, network partition)

Proposed timeline:
- Week 0 (this week): mutual agreement on scope + sign non-binding pilot MOU
- Week 1: infra access + sample data ingestion
- Week 2: run sync + chaos test; collect metrics
- Week 3-4: iterate and finalize runbook; produce short post-mortem

Can you confirm willingness to participate and (a) whether Pinecone or Weaviate prefers to own the primary index role for the pilot, and (b) if Acme can provision a test bucket by EOW? I copied Vanessa and Ben from our partnerships and product teams to keep the commercial and technical track aligned.

Attachments: [attachment: pilot-scope.pdf (PDF, 480KB)], [attachment: SOW-draft.docx (DOCX, 92KB)]

Thanks —
Dylan
Dylan Brooks
Head of Alliances, Redwood Inference
dylan.brooks@redwood.com

From: Emily Zhang <emily@pinecone.io>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 03 Aug 2027 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Edge storage + vector-sync partner pilot proposal

Dylan —

Thanks for the clear outline and the doc. Pinecone is interested in participating. We can spin up a sandbox project for the pilot (60GB capacity, dev tier) and assign an engineer to support the integration. For the primary index role: Pinecone can act as the authoritative, searchable store during the pilot — our team is more familiar with the metadata semantics you called out, and it simplifies the rollback story.

A few quick clarifying Qs from our side:
1) Can you share a representative blob format you plan to spill to S3 (JSON lines? Parquet?).
2) For restore, do you expect partial segment replay or full-segment rehydration?
3) Any compliance flags re: EU data touched during tests? (we prefer to keep pilot data in US region)

If you can answer those 3 items I’ll route to infra for sandbox provisioning. We can also set a short technical kickoff with our engineer (cc’d: Aman on my team will join) later this week.

—Emily
Emily Zhang
Partner Engineering, Pinecone
emily@pinecone.io
[attachment: pinecone-sandbox-invite.txt (TXT, 1KB)]

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
To: Emily Zhang <emily@pinecone.io>, Oscar Meier <oscar@weaviate.com>, Samir Gupta <samir@acme-storage.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 04 Aug 2027 09:34:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Edge storage + vector-sync partner pilot proposal

Emily — perfect, glad Pinecone can own the primary index role for the pilot. Answers inline below, and a few commercial notes for Vanessa/Ben to consider: 

1) Blob format: we plan to use compressed JSON Lines (one vector record per line) for portability; will also attach a small Parquet export for larger throughput testing. See sync-architecture.png in the attachments for the container layout.
2) Restore mode: pilot will exercise both partial segment (requested buckets of vectors) and full-segment rehydration — we'll start with partial for speed and move to full for endurance tests.
3) Compliance: pilot data will be synthetic US-only data (no PII). We will pin resources to US regions; if Weaviate wants to run EU tests later we can separate that into a follow-up.

Commercial asks: Vanessa/Ben — can we offer pilot credits to cover the sandbox dev tier + Acme ingress waiver? Suggested ask: Redwood covers baseline client traffic and engineering hours; Pinecone/Weaviate provide sandbox resources at no charge; Acme provides a temporary ingress/egress waiver for up to 2TB of pilot transfer. Ben — I can take point on a simple MOU if you’re OK.

Proposed next steps:
- Emily: route infra access; propose 2x 30-min tech kickoff slots (Thu/Fri)
- Samir: can Acme provision a US-west near-edge bucket and share creds (short-lived)?
- Vanessa/Ben: happy to sync 1:1 on commercial ask and MOU draft

Attachments referenced: [attachment: sync-architecture.png (PNG, 220KB)]

Thanks all —
Dylan

Quick notes after reading the SOW draft:
- Commercial: I’m OK with the pilot credits as long as we define a clear exit clause (30 days) and cap partner credit exposure (e.g., Pinecone sandbox only covers infra, not higher-tier support). Add a one-paragraph clause that pilot is non-binding and any ongoing commercial terms will be negotiated in a separate SOW.
- Legal / procurement: Laura, please flag any regulatory/clause issues. We’ll need a short MOU for signature to get Acme to lift the ingress fees.
- Metrics: add one operational metric — successful restore ratio (per-file) >= 99.5% during tests.

I’ll draft a one-page MOU and upload to Drive. Dylan — once you confirm the technical kickoff time with Emily, I’ll circulate the MOU and a simplified finance checklist.

Ben Carter
Director, Partnerships, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com
